list.title: Spectacle devices
list.intro: `"spectacle": { "at", "of", "device", "why" }` · the film NOMINATES its one loud moment. `device` is written as a shader sting at `at`, above the film; the other half is what makes it real, because with a spectacle declared the engine pulls EVERY competing amplitude dial down to 55% (other stings, seams, look strength, glow/beam intensity, kick scale) and exempts the layer named by `of`. Naming the peak is a promise the rest stays restrained. `core/spectacle.js`.
list.noPreview: a spectacle is a whole film turning its other dials down. One clip cannot show the restraint that makes it work.

list.title: Composite looks (static)
list.intro: `filter:"<look>"` · a colour-grade / treatment on a layer (STATIC). One positional arg is always strength (`"neon:0.9"`); the rest ride in `lookOpts`. **`strength` is the only knob every look takes** · `color` (recolours glow, streak, leak, wash and light), `color2` (the other side of a colour split), `colors` (gradient-map stops), `grain` and `vignette` each need the matching pass, so they apply to some looks and not others. A knob a look cannot apply THROWS and names what that look does take, rather than being silently dropped; `liveKnobs(name)` in `core/looks.js` is the list.
list.noPreview: a grade needs a photographic source, and the index ships no photographs. See it on the looks clip on /showcase.

entries.name: angelic
entries.desc: blown out, desaturated, the widest bloom in the library and an INVERTED vignette that whitens the corners · heaven light, heavy-handed by design

entries.name: chrome
entries.desc: specular highlights ADDED on top, then remapped to a navy/steel/white tritone · polished metal; two SVG filter passes, the most expensive look here

entries.name: crt
entries.desc: half the split of vhs plus a white bloom and the densest, darkest scanlines, corners pulled down · a lit phosphor tube: vhs glows and closes in

entries.name: cyberpunk
entries.desc: saturated hard, magenta/cyan split, magenta bloom over faint scanlines · a fixed neon-noir palette laid over your colours

entries.name: dreamSequence
entries.desc: the mildest warp plus defocus, cream bloom and a warm wash · dreamyHaze with the picture set drifting

entries.name: dreamyHaze
entries.desc: half-pixel defocus under a wide white bloom and a cream wash · soft-focus romance, no grain and no edges

entries.name: droneCinematic
entries.desc: every dial turned down (0.5 default strength, faint grain, shallow vignette) · a grade rather than a look, safe under type and product UI

entries.name: edgeGlow
entries.desc: flat areas cancel to black and only boundaries survive, amplified 6x and bloomed · a neon wire drawing; six passes, and a smooth subject can come out empty

entries.name: emboss
entries.desc: the kernel turns the picture into a grey lit rubbing and half the colour is thrown away · carved surface, per-pixel and not cheap

entries.name: fadedPolaroid
entries.desc: eight passes: sepia, desaturated, contrast LOWERED, brown wash, corner leak, grain, vignette · a print left in the sun, the flattest look here

entries.name: fatten
entries.desc: dilation swells the bright pixels into their neighbours · type gains weight and a photo goes chunky and poster-like

entries.name: filmNoir
entries.desc: full grayscale, contrast crushed up, a small white bloom, grain and the deepest vignette · monochrome drama

entries.name: glassWarp
entries.desc: medium-frequency turbulence pushes the image around behind a faint white bloom · seen through thick glass, still readable

entries.name: glitchGlow
entries.desc: wide 3px red/blue split, source-coloured bloom, sparse scanlines · hologram with the tint removed and the split doubled: a signal fault, not a projection

entries.name: halationFilm
entries.desc: warm amber bloom off the highlights plus grain, contrast barely touched · the restrained glow: no blur, no vignette, colours survive

entries.name: heatWarp
entries.desc: coarser, larger displacement under an orange wash and a lift · air over tarmac

entries.name: hologram
entries.desc: pink/cyan split, cyan flood-bloom and tight scanlines · a projected image, colour forced to teal

entries.name: impact
entries.desc: overexposed with the widest colour split here (4px) and a white bloom · the frame taking a punch, for one frozen hit only

entries.name: letterpress
entries.desc: diffuse light multiplies the image so it sinks into a warm paper wash, lifted 1.5x to stop it going black · ink pressed into stock

entries.name: lomo
entries.desc: the strongest saturation and the heaviest vignette in the library, plus a corner leak and grain · plastic-camera punch: no glow, no split, just crush and corners

entries.name: melt
entries.desc: the lowest frequency and by far the largest displacement here · big slow lumps that destroy legibility, so never under type

entries.name: neon
entries.desc: the bright parts bloom in their OWN colours, nothing is tinted · real sign-light, the one glow look that keeps the palette

entries.name: nightVision
entries.desc: grayscale then sepia then hue-rotated and saturated 4x to ONE green, green bloom, lines, grain, vignette · image intensifier; the original colour is gone, not tinted

entries.name: nostalgia
entries.desc: fadedPolaroid without the wash, the flattening or the vignette, plus a warm bloom · same memory register, lighter and open at the edges

entries.name: rippleGlass
entries.desc: the highest frequency and a small offset, so the distortion reads as tight ripples not lumps, over a cool bloom · water on the lens

entries.name: super8
entries.desc: sepia, lifted, the heaviest grain here and a deep vignette · warmth and dirt only, no split and no lines: film stock, not video

entries.name: thermal
entries.desc: luminance remapped to a six-stop black-purple-pink-orange-white ramp, softened · a heat camera; three passes, the cheapest sci-fi look and the most total recolour

entries.name: timeFreeze
entries.desc: drained of colour, washed cold blue with a matching bloom and a hairline split · the world stopped

entries.name: vhs
entries.desc: colour split 3px, slight defocus, scanlines and heavy grain · tape: no vignette and no glow, so the frame stays flat and dirty

entries.name: vintageAnamorphic
entries.desc: the only look with horizontal blue streaks off the highlights, plus split, grain and a deep vignette · old spherical glass

entries.name: watercolor
entries.desc: displaced, desaturated, contrast lowered under a multiplied paper wash and grain · pigment on stock

list.title: Layer types
list.intro: The vocabulary itself: `{ "type":"<name>" }`. Everything else in this document is a dial ON one of these. Full props per type: `formats/scene/schema.json`, and `docs/PRIMITIVES.md` for what each is FOR.
list.noPreview: a layer type is the noun, not the effect. Every preview on this page is already one of them.

list.title: three.js scenes (real geometry)
list.intro: `{ "type":"three", "three":"<name>" }` · a scene graph: meshes, materials, lights, a camera. For what a distance field structurally cannot express: a font outline, a device body, a captured UI plane, a point cloud. Deterministic by contract · every object is POSED ABSOLUTELY from t, never stepped by delta (`core/three-fx.js`), and `make canvas-purity` hashes the real pixels to prove it.

list.title: Raymarched surfaces

list.title: Layer-as-texture (resample)
list.intro: `"resample":{ "fx":"", "amount":[from,to] }` · bind a layer that is already a raster (a canvas or an ``) as a GL texture and re-sample it through a fragment shader. This is the family that needs to SEE pixels: real lens distortion, radial and spin blur.
list.noPreview: resampling reads the pixels of a layer that is already a raster, so it needs a real image to sample.

entries.name: bitCrush
entries.desc: quantise the palette down until it bands, each 0.25 of `amount` halving the bit depth · a degrade beat, never decoration

entries.name: chromaShift
entries.desc: radial RGB separation, the channels pulling apart from the centre outwards

entries.name: dissolve
entries.desc: noise-thresholded erosion lit by an ember front · the way OUT of an image; ramp `amount:[0.05, 0.95]` to burn it away

entries.name: fisheye
entries.desc: real lens distortion: barrel above the middle of the dial, pincushion below, `0.5` the identity · outside the source reads empty, never a stretched edge

entries.name: macroblock
entries.desc: the flat blocks and dropped tiles of a starved codec · a glitch/degrade beat, never decoration

entries.name: refract
entries.desc: liquid glass: the image BENDS along a noise gradient with per-channel dispersion and a specular glint · what a blur cannot do

entries.name: spinBlur
entries.desc: smear along the arc with the radius preserved, so the pivot itself stays sharp · a rotating badge or seal

entries.name: zoomBlur
entries.desc: radial smear out from the centre, near samples kept crisp · an impact moment; ramp `amount:[0.6, 0]` so the frame rushes in and snaps sharp

list.title: Ambient shader fields
list.intro: `{ "type":"shader", "shader":"<name>" }` · a full-frame generative field, pure in t, palette-tintable via `colors`. Sits behind content; no sampler, so it cannot read what is under it.

entries.name: aurora
entries.desc: drifting colour aurora (moves)

list.title: Filter presets
list.intro: `filter:"<name>"` · a named colour grade. Composite LOOKS are the richer set above; these are the primitives.
list.noPreview: a colour grade needs a photographic source, and the index ships no photographs.

entries.name: bloom
entries.desc: thresholds LUMINANCE and blooms the bright parts at two scales · light comes out of the picture, so a dark edge emits nothing. `ry` makes it directional (an anamorphic streak)

entries.name: chromaGlow
entries.desc: a stack of zero-offset drop-shadows: white core, warm mid halo, cool outer. It follows the ALPHA, so it is right on GLYPHS and wrong on an opaque picture, where it haloes the rectangle. For a photo use `bloom`

entries.name: chromaSplit
entries.desc: the colour channels pulled apart per pixel and summed back · real fringing on the picture, not a coloured silhouette of its alpha. `warm`/`cool` tint each direction

entries.name: convolve
entries.desc: a 3x3 kernel reading NEIGHBOURING pixels: emboss (a lit rubbing), edge (flat areas cancel to black, only boundaries survive), sharpen

entries.name: displace
entries.desc: static turbulence drives a displacement map · the pixels are pushed around by a fixed noise field. `freq` sets lump size (low = few big lumps), `scale` sets how far

entries.name: duotone
entries.desc: luminance remapped to TWO colours, shadows to highlights · the poster/press look; defaults to --ink and --accent, so it reskins per theme

entries.name: gradientMap
entries.desc: luminance remapped across any number of stops · the general case the two above are special cases of: a heat ramp, a risograph, a false-colour read

entries.name: morph
entries.desc: dilate or erode · swell the bright pixels into their neighbours, or eat them away. Type gains or loses weight

entries.name: posterize
entries.desc: each channel quantised to N discrete levels IN PLACE, hues kept · banding as a decision, not an artefact

entries.name: relief
entries.desc: a light source over a luminance bump map. Diffuse MULTIPLIES (ink pressed into stock), specular ADDS (a highlight on metal): same primitive, opposite composite

entries.name: sepia
entries.desc: the plain CSS sepia, an amount 0..1 · the cheapest warm-and-dated pass there is

entries.name: tritone
entries.desc: duotone with a third stop in the middle, which is what stops the midtones going muddy

entries.name: vignette
entries.desc: NOT a filter · a darkening field composited over the layer box, so it is an inset radial-gradient overlay div and stays sharp at the edges

entries.name: arch
entries.desc: a sine hump · it leaves the baseline at a finite slope and its shoulders sag, so it reads as a bump, not a dome

entries.name: bottom
entries.desc: as an anchor, the element grows up from the bottom edge and its free end is the top; as a direction, away is downward

entries.name: bottom-left
entries.desc: a diagonal fall away to the bottom left · light rarely leaves along an axis, and no edge keyword says this

entries.name: bottom-right
entries.desc: a diagonal fall away to the bottom right · light rarely leaves along an axis, and no edge keyword says this

entries.name: breathe
entries.desc: idle breathe

entries.name: center
entries.desc: a radial: away in EVERY direction at once, so no edge can darken without the others darkening too

entries.name: circle
entries.desc: the unit semicircular arc, which leaves the baseline UPRIGHT · a symmetric dome, a planet limb, an eclipse

entries.name: crescent
entries.desc: one circular arc with a second equal arc bitten out of it · a moon horn: empty on one side, a concave inner edge, a point at the tip

entries.name: drift
entries.desc: the field travels as one body, the cells holding station against each other

entries.name: full
entries.desc: the no-op envelope, 1 everywhere: every element runs the whole frame, which is what a blind does

entries.name: hills
entries.desc: three gaussians of unequal width and height summed · rolling ground: three summits with soft saddles between them

entries.name: left
entries.desc: a linear fall away to the left · a direction and no centre, so only the move along it reaches the fall

entries.name: left-and-right
entries.desc: a lit vertical band with darkness at both sides and nothing taken off the top or bottom

entries.name: ramp
entries.desc: a straight climb across the row, so the extents rise steadily from one side to the other

entries.name: right
entries.desc: a linear fall away to the right · the default bearing

entries.name: rings
entries.desc: concentric bands round a point, like light on water · the eye travels outwards

entries.name: scallops
entries.desc: the same semicircle repeated five times. Odd, so one arc sits centred · a scalloped horizon when shallow, an arcade when tall

entries.name: shards
entries.desc: a fan of rays from a pivot below the frame · the eye travels up and out

entries.name: shimmer
entries.desc: the cells slide against each other, so the seams open and close

entries.name: slats
entries.desc: a backlit blind: vertical bars of unequal width, each with a lit leading edge falling to a dark trailing edge · the eye travels across

entries.name: still
entries.desc: nothing moves: the output reads no clock at all

entries.name: top
entries.desc: as an anchor, the element hangs down from the top edge and its free end is the bottom; as a direction, away is upward

entries.name: top-and-bottom
entries.desc: a lit band across the middle with darkness above and below it and nothing taken off the sides · the shape a low sun makes

entries.name: top-left
entries.desc: a diagonal fall away to the top left · light rarely leaves along an axis, and no edge keyword says this

entries.name: top-right
entries.desc: a diagonal fall away to the top right · light rarely leaves along an axis, and no edge keyword says this

entries.name: valley
entries.desc: the sine hump run upside down: a dip in the middle with both ends tall

entries.name: wave
entries.desc: sinusoidal wave across units
